request.deadline: Three-month staged launch-liquidity deployment after enactment, with monthly reporting; broader final delivery deadline not stated in document
deliverables: Shared BTC reserve architecture with transparent safety mechanisms and reserve-ratio rules
Composable Cardano-native FIRE and ICE assets
Open-source SDKs and adapters for wallets, DEXs, and DeFi protocols
Always-on public dashboards for reserve ratio, asset supply, liquidity health, fee flows, and deployment status
Monthly governance reports and reporting standards
Independent security review, audit, and economic modeling
Legal/compliance work, disclosures, treasury reporting, and launch-readiness review
request.recipient: Sundial Protocol and Charms, with Intersect proposed as interim fund administrator subject to confirmation and final agreement.
request.what: Fund Alchemy, a Cardano-native Bitcoin treasury protocol and BTCfi infrastructure layer with reserve architecture, FIRE and ICE assets, dashboards, integration adapters, reporting, audits, administration, legal/compliance work, go-to-market execution, and staged launch liquidity.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 10,000,000 ada using an approximate USD 0.20 per ada reference value for an approximately USD 2.0 million planning budget split into two approximately USD 1.0 million pools.

Pool 1 is intended for protocol infrastructure and staged launch liquidity, kept separate from operating spend, deployed in three monthly tranches, and designed to return profits, yield, and returns to the Cardano Treasury quarterly.

Pool 2 is intended to fund delivery, audit, integrations, dashboards, governance reporting, legal/compliance work, and go-to-market execution with itemized planning allocations totaling approximately USD 1.0 million.
Alchemy proposes a shared BTC reserve architecture where FIRE and ICE are backed by the same BTC reserve, with formulas for reserve ratio and FIRE price and an initial target reserve ratio of 5.0x.
The proposal says safety zones will constrain minting and redemption above 4.0x, between 2.0x and 4.0x, and below 2.0x reserve ratio to protect reserve integrity and reduce overleveraging risk.
FIRE is described as a volatility-absorbing residual BTC-backed claim with amplified upside and first-loss downside, while ICE is described as lower-volatility USD-denominated BTC-backed exposure.

The document asserts that Cardano currently lacks a production BTCfi infrastructure layer and that Alchemy would provide reusable Cardano BTCfi infrastructure for wallets, DEXs, DeFi protocols, dashboards, and future builders.

The document cites external references and market examples, including Strategy Q1 2026 results and other Bitcoin-backed products, to support the claim that demand for structured Bitcoin exposure is meaningful and growing.

The proposal includes treasury protections including no DRep funds or personal compensation to Sundial or Charms principals, a rollover commitment if external investment funds development, ADA price protection above USD 0.35, pause rules, and refund or return conditions.

The proposal acknowledges risks from BTC volatility, oracle, bridge, Charms protocol-layer vulnerabilities, novel asset treatment, delivery, and adoption, and proposes mitigations including audit, modeling, staged deployment, dashboards, legal/compliance work, reporting, and administrator oversight.

summary: The document requests 10,000,000 ada for a Sundial x Charms BTCfi infrastructure proposal with separated launch-liquidity and delivery pools, staged deployment, reporting, audits, dashboards, integrations, treasury return mechanisms, and several stated governance controls. The strongest support is for the internal budget structure, technical design, and proposed controls; adoption and market-demand claims rely partly on proposer assertions and externally checkable references.
